request.state:
Assess changes to migration boundaries for Can packages at30e211dae891cfdca3f6322ce45c46c426138830. The goal is simpler useful Rust adoption, preserved workflows/evaluation/permissions and lower interop maintenance. Only existing packages/ source may be ported; compiler changes are excluded and directories must name responsibilities. New internal contracts can coexist with unchanged legacy APIs but cannot silently narrow them. There is no implementation or fresh performance experiment. Previous7/5/7/7 judgments cover existing narrow arithmetic/full validator/work-helper/artifact-helper scopes, not these new proposals.
A values operation can own carriers/exact math, AST/prepared schemas and whole decode-check-normalize-encode or batch aggregate computation. Current fields already contain ASTs and repeated leaf/union string parsing can be eliminated even in TS. HTTP JSON/form parsers produce fresh data consumed by framing and bounds; interfaces bound checking/MCP has actual consumers including values datetime validation. That does not guarantee arbitrary in-process/SDK objects are inert. A parser-private owned token can admit a new domain with no accessors/proxies/holes/functions/cycles, while legacy unknown traversal continues TS access/identity semantics. Retain UTF16 surrogates, key order/proto data, numeric transport, omission and profile-specific errors; opaque Can json is unsuitable as a blanket DTO because it rejects every number. Keep values in Rust only across an actual internal multi-stage workflow, materializing once when JS needs BigInts/fields; handles alone cannot migrate emitted expression chains without excluded lowering changes. State hash/replay precedes age/authority/checks, so defaults/decoding must remain later; profiles differ for interface first-error presence, values collected violations and state15digit positive versions. Canonical receipt serialization additionally has observable toJSON/getter behavior and JS number/key rendering; strict owned data is a new path rather than equivalence to that full API.
Work policy lives across work row/transition helpers, restated state fanout tables, state outcome/checkpoint staging, and actual Cloudflare durable adapters. Work's in-memory child store is explicitly test only. Share codecs+transition/receipt/recovery logic+batch linkage assertions as a bounded native core, keeping individual package error profiles and producers. The host retains DB operations, guards/membership/provider calls and atomic fences. Avoid consolidating intentionally different orchestration traces indiscriminately. A later resumable Rust session can own control flow while requesting load/query/fresh checkpoint/snapshot/guard/authority/invoke then a conditional batch; keep exceptions, callback demand, act-time rereads, caller retries and single commit. Taking all DB/auth/provider implementations is a much larger project. Declarative state row filters/sort/projection/aggregates can reuse decoded rows later, but visibility projection must precede where and existing f64/limit behavior remains. Whole migration validation includes JS invariant callbacks, so its data checks must be extracted first.
For artifacts, one native local preparation job can retain artifact metadata/indexes, release inventory, typed module graph, compatibility, plans, review/diffs/rendered JSON/TOML and binary-safe staging. Existing JS helpers already share a process; isolated Rust replacements would add the crossings one wishes to avoid. Retain first diagnostics, unknown/additive fields, UTF16 JS/map content, ordered bindings/reasons, exact escaping/hash version and unmapped schedules. Current dist manifests already cover arbitrary byte files. Bundle generation uses Bun to build real MCP code and interfaces-owned catalog derivation for derived-inputs.js. Pass prebuilt outputs or call a single JS build adapter; leave Bun bundling, producer activation and Wrangler apply intact. Duplicate interface derivation or replace the whole platform/Worker to remove that last adapter increases scope. Native preparation returns compact review/result data, owns graph/buffers, and preserves no deployment-file writes during preview plus reviewed bytes through write/apply. Distribution remains cost; hashing already uses native Node crypto. Shared typed Wasm asset/loading/reproducibility work and target tests can help runtime cores independently of porting local preparation. No claimed speedup is measured.

values_boundary.instructions: Choose the most useful next boundary strategy for values arithmetic and validation, weighing lower data/callback crossing and shared authority against compatibility, scope and upkeep. Preserve stated old behaviors and workflows; do not presume performance improvement or obligatory Rust adoption.

criteria.owned_pipeline: A shared exact-value/codec/plan core operates on internally parser-owned data in complete checking/encoding calls, while old unknown APIs retain JS compatibility. Concrete callers and amortized transfer improve the boundary; maintain distinct profiles, lossless text and measured TS comparison.
criteria.legacy_full_port: One larger Rust values backend supports all current exports without changing any input/read/identity behavior. Broader native ownership is valuable but requires the difficult host-read bridge as well as shipping.
criteria.ts_preparation: Prepare structured TS validation and codec dispatch behind present APIs, measuring consumers before a port. Cheaper adoption and compatibility; native reuse and Rust-owned values are delayed.

work_boundary.instructions: Choose the most useful next boundary strategy for work/state lifecycle and recovery, weighing lower data/callback crossing and shared authority against compatibility, scope and upkeep. Preserve stated old behaviors and workflows; do not presume performance improvement or obligatory Rust adoption.

criteria.transition_core: Port shared row/transition/receipt/recovery and batch-link rules across work/state, leaving IO/live checks/final commit in TS. Concrete duplication disappears; orchestration still crosses and per-owner outputs need compatibility.
criteria.resumable_commands: Extend that core to resumable Rust command/scheduler state, driving exact host requests through TS. Retained intermediate state reduces repeated row transfer, at higher sequencing/error/retry protocol cost.
criteria.whole_runtime: Move all work/state storage, authorization/invocation and providers to Rust together. Removes more seams but greatly expands platform and transaction/permission verification.
criteria.ts_consolidation: Share policy and codecs in the current language first. Improves consistency with few build changes, but no native multi-runtime core or bridge measurement.

artifact_boundary.instructions: Choose the most useful next boundary strategy for local artifact and deployment preparation, weighing lower data/callback crossing and shared authority against compatibility, scope and upkeep. Preserve stated old behaviors and workflows; do not presume performance improvement or obligatory Rust adoption.

criteria.owned_preparation: Native preparation owns artifact/release/module/compat/plan/review/output data, using built outputs or one JS builder and retaining producer activation/Wrangler. Coarse operation supports reuse; exact bytes/errors and multi-platform shipping need proof.
criteria.helper_exports: Translate the existing artifact/check/plan functions individually with JS call wrappers. Small reversible tranches, but frequent ownership transfers and the workflow remains host-driven.
criteria.full_platform: Take local CLI, bundler and Worker/deployment subsystems into a comprehensive Rust platform. Large native scope and fewer JS crossings, with substantial extra integrations and no evidence they are needed.
criteria.ts_asset_upgrade: Retain TS prepare while making assets/manifests/loaders binary-aware. Practical enabling work for values/work Wasm with low local disruption, but no native prepare operation.
